DRIFTING UNTETHERED — body turned slow at a diagonal, arms spread wide, safety tether trailing in a loose curve behind, helmet tipped toward the world below.
REACHING FOR A LOST TOOL — one arm fully extended after a wrench tumbling just beyond gloved fingertips, the other anchored to a handrail, legs floating free.
WELDING A HULL BREACH — braced upside-down against the plating, plasma-cutter throwing a fan of white sparks that drift and die in the vacuum.
PUSHING OFF THE HULL — both boots planted mid-shove, body launching backward into the void, tether snapping taut in a lazy arc.
TUMBLING SLOWLY END-OVER-END — body rotating heel-over-helmet in full free-fall, arms tucked close, the station and the planet trading places with every slow revolution.
HAULING HAND-OVER-HAND — gloves gripping a guide-wire in alternating pulls, body horizontal and flying low along the truss, boots skimming nothing but shadow.
ANCHORING A CABLE — torso twisted hard at the waist, both hands driving a tether bolt into a truss fitting, knees bent and floating at an angle.
HANGING HEAD-DOWN — body inverted above the planet's curve, one boot hooked in a foot restraint, both hands free and working a panel below the horizon.
RETRIEVING A DRIFTING CRATE — arms outstretched in a slow lunge, fingers closing around a cargo handle, body arcing gently on a bent tether toward the tumbling box.
BRACING AGAINST THRUSTER RECOIL — maneuvering unit firing a short burst, body shoved sideways in free-fall, legs splayed, one arm thrown out to absorb the invisible kick.
CRADLING A RECOVERED COMPONENT — floating at a diagonal, both arms wrapped around a salvaged circuit assembly pressed to the chest, legs drifting loose behind in a wide V.
INSPECTING A GLOWING INSTRUMENT — face-plate pressed close to a pulsing readout panel, body horizontal and hovering, one hand steadying on a bracket, knees bent upward.
REACHING THE APEX OF A TETHER ARC — body fully suspended at the farthest point of swing, arms wide, tether pulled taut beneath, the station impossibly far below booted feet.
TWISTING TO LOOK BACK — torso rotating over one shoulder toward the viewer, one arm still gripping a handhold, legs drifting ahead at a loose diagonal in the glare.
CUTTING A HULL PANEL — body wedged sideways against the exterior, cutting torch drawing a bright orange line across the plating, molten droplets beading off into the black.
COILING A LOOSE TETHER — floating upright at a slight tilt, both gloved hands gathering slack line into a spiral loop, boots hovering well above any surface.
WRESTLING A STUCK HATCH — both arms yanking a recessed handle, body bent backward in weightless strain, feet braced on nothing, hips torquing the full effort into the pull.
PHOTOGRAPHING DAMAGE UP CLOSE — camera pressed to the visor, body hovering at an oblique angle over a scorched panel, one boot hooked loosely in a nearby rung.
SIGNALING WITH A RAISED FIST — one arm thrust overhead in a thumbs-up, body drifting on a slow spin, tether looping in a long S-curve back toward the airlock.
THREADING A CABLE THROUGH A DUCT — one arm buried elbow-deep into an open truss cavity, body twisted perpendicular to the hull, legs floating out at a wide diagonal.
SOMERSAULTING DELIBERATELY — tucked tight into a ball, pulling both knees to the chest, spinning in a controlled roll as the planet slides across the helmet visor.
PLANTING A FOOT RESTRAINT — body inverted, both hands hammering a gold clamp onto a rung, legs splayed upward in a wide V against the star field.
CATCHING A FLOATING BOLT — eyes locked on a tumbling fastener, one glove open and intercepting its slow drift, body braced at a tilt on the fingertips of the other hand.
REELING IN A SLACK SAFETY LINE — body leaning back in free-fall, both arms pulling hand-over-hand on the tether, the reel spinning on the suit's hip in lazy arcs.
FLOATING STILL IN A SUNBEAM — body at a long diagonal, no handholds taken, arms loose at the sides, visor catching full golden light as the terminator creeps slowly beneath.
